parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file sits in the application layer because of its *.service.ts name. Its main job is to coordinate saving a file record through FileRepository, which does fit the application role. But FilesLocalService.create also does HTTP transport work. It throws UnprocessableEntityException and puts HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY inside the error body, so the HTTP status code is decided inside the use case. It takes an Express.Multer.File, which is a type from the web framework. It also builds the public URL by hand from the 'app.apiPrefix' config and a hard-coded '/v1/' route version, which means it depends on how the API is routed. Status codes, framework upload types and route layout are presentation or transport concerns, not use-case orchestration. The local folder path also suggests this is really an infrastructure upload adapter that has been labelled as application. Many NestJS projects do this, so my confidence is only moderate. Under the rubric, though, transport logic in a file outside the presentation layer counts as a misplaced responsibility.
